correctness.rationale: Parseval provides the exact row collision integral. A uniform Gaussian comparison follows from logarithmic binomial-vs-exponential control and sin(t/2) bounds, valid at every interior mesh point. The sum of errors is dominated by min(j,n-j)^(-3/2). A Bernoulli–Poisson coupling of order j^2/n and singular-mesh zeta summation yield the absolute O(n^-1/7) remainder. The packaged checker independently matches 12 exact small matrix energies and five Poisson collision integrals; finite observations are not used to prove the limit.

value.rationale: The unweighted Hilbert–Schmidt energy is a natural spectral statistic of the canonical Bernstein approximation collocation operator. Bulk Gaussian approximations alone do not recover the order-one correction because two Poisson edges survive; the theorem gives the exact constant (zeta plus two Bessel sums), all-degree universality, and a quantitative convergence rate, rather than an arbitrary finite instance. It may inform studies of discrete Bernstein operator spectral energy and mesh-dependent asymptotics; no downstream theorem is claimed.
